messages:
sara: Heads up — over the last 40m we've seen NVMe controller resets on a subset of gnodes in eu-west3 during heavy GPU preemption windows. Affected hosts show `fsync` errors and `writeback` stalls, some OOM-kill churn.
liam: ugh. any pattern on models/jobs?
sara: Mostly during big batch job teardown when we preempt GPUs for the reclaim step. I attached a small log excerpt: ```kernel: nvmectrl 0000:3b:00.0: controller reset due to fatal error
kern: FSYNC failed: -5 (EIO) writeback_sync returned -5
containerd: oom_reaper killed process pid=24567 ```
mei: that log looks like controller reset triggered by firmware power-capping? vendor firmware v2.3 had a known bug for concurrent cache flush + power drop. are those nodes on the newer image?
sara: yes, these are the eu-west3 preemptible pools we rolled last week onto image-7.2 which includes the vendor fw.
devon: can we repro locally by forcing heavy KV-cache flushes + preemption? want to avoid mass evicts while we investigate.
ops-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-1387. Pager duty alerted.
liam: short-term mitigation: disable aggressive preemption for queued batch jobs in eu-west3 and reduce parallelism for teardown so we don't hammer the NVMe. will that hurt capacity?
sara: it does — expect ~12% slower reclaim, so GPU provisioning latency goes up. tradeoff is fewer broken hosts.
mei: long term we should coordinate vendor firmware rollback or apply their hotfix. also add a kernel patch that retries fsyncs on EIO from nvme controller reset instead of immediate container OOM.
devon: I'll open a GH issue and a patch PR for the fsync retry + exponential backoff. putting a temporary host label `no-preempt-scrub` on the eu-west3 pools now.
vendor-bot: Vendor ticket #VEND-8245 opened referencing fw v2.3 controller-reset under flush+powercap. ETA 3d for microcode patch.
liam: ops plan: 1) toggle preemption throttle, 2) reduce teardown parallelism, 3) add host label to avoid scheduling sensitive jobs, 4) vendor engagement + kernel retry PR. I'll ping infra-sre for rollout plan.
sara: posting a short runbook in #eng-oncall with mitigation steps and a script to label nodes: ```./label-nodes --region eu-west3 --label no-preempt-scrub```
mei: also add a metric alert on nvme_controller_resets and fsync_error_rate to catch recurrence.
devon: created GH #1246 with test case and draft patch. linking INF-2026-1387 and VEND-8245.
liam: nice. estimate: we absorb provisioning latency hit for 48h, monitor, then apply vendor microcode to a canary subset.
sara: thanks all, I'll follow up with the incident doc later. :thumbsup:
